beats.text: Fifteen percent of men have zero close friends. Back in nineteen ninety? Three percent.
A national survey asked two thousand Americans how many close friends they have.
That's five times as many men with nobody. And it's not just the zeros.
Men with six or more close friends dropped from fifty-five percent to twenty-seven.
And last week, forty-one percent of women got emotional support from a friend. Men? Twenty-one.
So if your circle got smaller, you're not the exception. You're the trend.

sources: Survey Center on American Life (June 2021), 'The State of American Friendship: Change, Challenges, and Loss' (American Perspectives Survey, May 14-23, 2021, 2,019 US adults, MOE +/-2.4). Women vs men who received emotional support from a friend in the past week: 41% vs 21%. Via americansurveycenter.org.

Men with no close friends 3% (1990) vs 15% (2021); men with 6+ close friends 55% (1990) vs 27% (2021): Daniel Cox (director of the Survey Center), Art of Manliness podcast #726 (July 2021), also reported by The Week (2021).
